findings: "unknown" protection status is unreachable — _map_device() never emits "unknown" but WatchGuardDevice["protection_status"] still includes it as a union member and ProtectionBadge has a dead default arm for it. Either restore a fallback that emits "unknown" for unrecognised isolation_state values, or remove it from the union.

All non-isolated, non-reinstall devices are classified "protected" — the new logic drops agentStatus-based detection and uses only reinstall_protection_requested / reinstall_agent_requested as error signals. Any device in a genuinely degraded state that doesn't set those flags will show as protected. Confirm these two flags are the complete degraded-state signal set for WatchGuard Cloud, or extend the mapping.

License counter [{}][0] swallows an empty list — lic_data.get("product_license_counter", [{}])[0] raises IndexError when the API returns "product_license_counter": [] (empty array), not a missing key. The outer except catches it silently and the card shows 0 with no indication of failure. Fix: (lic_data.get("product_license_counter") or [{}])[0].

EncryptionBadge silent mismatch on unmapped values — if the backend ever emits an encryption value not in the {none, BitLocker, BitLocker+TPM} set (e.g. type 4), EncryptionBadge falls through to its catch-all and renders it as a green badge indistinguishable from a valid encrypted state. Low severity while the type union is closed, but worth adding an explicit unknown/fallback arm.
